[maas-code-reviewer review]

> LLM-generated review from https://github.com/canonical/maas-code-reviewer.
> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


Solid, careful port of `maasserver/dhcp.py`'s config-gathering logic into the service layer; the clause factories, table mirror (`maasserver_interfacerelationship` matches `InterfaceRelationship` exactly), `ntp_external_only` key (the temporal activity's `use_external_ntp_only` is wrong), `relay_vlan_id` (vs. the never-populated `Vlan.relayed_vlan_id`), and the "no interface for a family ⇒ drop that family" rule all line up with legacy. Error handling is a genuine improvement over legacy (`ValidationException` instead of `AttributeError` on `None.ip`).

Five things I'd want addressed before merge:

1. **`KeaHAConfig` is not keyed by VLAN/family.** Legacy failover peers are `failover-vlan-%d` and are referenced per subnet pool. `ha_data` is a flat list with only rack system IDs + IPs, so an agent receiving two HA VLANs with the same rack pair cannot tell which peer belongs to which subnet, and `SubnetData.secondary_rack_system_id` is not enough to disambiguate. Add `vlan_id` (and `ip_version`).

2. **HA address selection diverges from legacy** (`_get_ip_address_for_rack_controller`, dhcp.py:542). Legacy `get_ip_address_for_rack_controller` restricts the candidate set to interfaces with STICKY/AUTO addresses whose subnet VLAN is *exactly* `vlan`, then picks the best. The new code reuses `_get_best_interface_with_ip_on_vlan`, whose candidate set also admits relay-VLAN addresses and DISCOVERED-only interfaces; if that "best" interface has no STICKY/AUTO on `vlan.id`, `None` is returned and the whole request fails with a ValidationException, where legacy would have picked a different interface.

3. **N+1 queries on a hot path.** DHCP data is regenerated on every relevant network change. `_get_best_interface_with_ip_on_vlan` is invoked once per subnet, and inside does one `get_for_interfaces([id])` per interface plus, per IP, a `subnets.get_by_id` and a full `ipranges.get_many` whose only use is `len()` — i.e. O(subnets x interfaces x ips) round trips, plus two more full rack scans per subnet for HA, plus a `get_source_address` + DNS resolution per subnet. Legacy achieves this with `prefetch_related`. Please memoize per `(vlan.id, ip_version)`, batch `get_for_interfaces(all_ids)`, and precompute a `subnet_id -> dynamic range count` map.

4. **Duplicate payload models.** `maastemporalworker/workflow/dhcp.py` already defines `DHCPDataForAgent`, `SubnetData`, `VlanData`, `InterfaceData`, `IPRangeData`, `HostReservationData` with different field sets (e.g. `HostReservationData` there carries `subnet_id`/`domain`). Nothing in this change migrates that activity, so two incompatible shapes for the same agent payload now coexist. Please state the cutover (or do it here) so they don't drift.

5. **`with_interface_enabled` has no `joins`.** It only works because `get_for_nodes` happens to join `InterfaceTable`; used with plain `get_many` it silently produces a cross join. `with_interface_ids` in the same factory shows the right pattern.

Security: nothing new. All predicates are SQLAlchemy-parameterized, the only external input is `system_id`, and `rack.url` fed to `urlparse`/`resolve_hostname` is admin-controlled, same as legacy.

src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.150: One query per VLAN to find relayed VLANs. Collapse to a single `relay_vlan_id IN (...)` lookup after the dict is built — the legacy `vlan.relay_vlans.all()` was prefetched.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.181: Redundant: `QuerySpec.enrich_stmt` already applies `order_by=[OrderByClause(IPRangeTable.c.id)]` (filters.py:108-112), so the rows arrive sorted by id. Drop this sort (or drop the `order_by` and keep the Python sort, but not both).
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.259: Legacy computes the best interface once per `(vlan, ip_version)` (`get_dhcp_configure_for`), not once per subnet. Here it is recomputed for every subnet, and each call rescans every rack interface with per-interface/per-IP queries. Memoize on `(vlan.id, subnet.cidr.version)`.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.263: `configured_ip_versions` is only updated when `iface.vlan_id is not None`. `Interface.vlan_id` is nullable, so a best interface without a VLAN silently drops *every* subnet of that address family from the payload. Legacy only checks `interface is not None`. Move the `add()` out of the `vlan_id` guard and keep the guard for `dhcp_interfaces` only.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.273: `KeaHAConfig` carries no VLAN id or IP version, so the agent cannot associate a failover peer with the subnets/pools that must reference it (legacy names peers `failover-vlan-%d` per VLAN and per family). Two HA VLANs sharing the same rack pair produce indistinguishable entries. Add `vlan_id` and `ip_version` to the dataclass.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.279: Unreachable: `_get_ha_config` on line 271 already raises when `vlan.primary_rack_id` is None, so `peer_rack_id` cannot be None here. Remove the branch or move the validation before the `_get_ha_config` call.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.304: `external_ntp` is assigned by reference into every `SubnetData.ntp_servers` and into the top-level `ntp_servers`, so all of them alias one list. Use `list(external_ntp)` to avoid surprising aliasing in consumers.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.370: This is the exact expression already evaluated into `default_dns_servers` above. Reuse the variable instead of recomputing the dict/generator.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.422: One query per interface, per subnet. `get_for_interfaces` already accepts a list — fetch all rack interface IDs once and group in memory.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.433: `get_many` materializes every dynamic IPRange row just to take `len()`, and runs once per IP address of every interface for every subnet. Use a single `subnet_id -> dynamic range count` aggregate (one `GROUP BY` query) computed up front; this mirrors legacy's `prefetch_related("ip_addresses__subnet__iprange_set")`.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.483: Redundant refetch: these addresses were already loaded in the loop above and stored as element `[1]` of the candidate tuples — which is otherwise never read (`for interface, _, _ in candidates`). Either use the stored list here or drop it from the tuple.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.542: Behavioural divergence from legacy `get_ip_address_for_rack_controller`. Legacy builds the candidate set only from interfaces with a STICKY/AUTO address on exactly `vlan`, then picks the best of those. `_get_best_interface_with_ip_on_vlan` also accepts relay-VLAN addresses and DISCOVERED-only interfaces, so the selected interface may have no STICKY/AUTO address on `vlan.id` at all — this returns None and `_get_ha_config` then aborts the entire request, where legacy would have found a usable interface. Filter candidates to `vlan.id` + sticky/auto before picking the best.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.564: Annotate: `hosts_by_subnet: dict[int, list[HostReservationData]] = {...}`. The empty-list literal leaves the value type unresolved for pyright, which `maasservicelayer` is expected to pass.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.607: Diverges from legacy `make_hosts_for_subnets`: legacy adds a parent to `interface_ids` only when it actually emits a host entry for it (same-MAC parents are skipped *without* being marked seen). Marking it seen here suppresses a legitimate host entry for that parent if it later shows up as a directly-addressed interface in the same group. Move `seen_interfaces.add(parent.id)` below the MAC comparison.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.666: `assert` for a DB-derived invariant in a production path — stripped under `python -O`, and an AssertionError surfaces as a 500 with no context. Prefer an explicit exception (or fall back to the `unknown-...` hostname). Same applies to the asserts at 432, 681/683 and 713/725.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.797: The `seen_regions` check runs *after* the per-region `get_for_nodes` query, so the query is executed and discarded. Move the check above it. Also, `regions_by_id` is built but only iterated via `.values()` — just iterate `regions`.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.829: `_get_default_dns_servers_for_subnet` is called once per subnet, and each call does a `get_source_address` plus a `resolve_hostname` on a worker thread. The resolution result depends only on `(maas_server_host, ip_version)` — memoize it for the duration of the request; otherwise a rack with many subnets issues one DNS lookup each.

src/maasservicelayer/models/dhcp.py.45: `gateway_ip: str` with `""` as the missing-value sentinel is lossy for a consumer that has to decide whether to emit a router option. `str | None` matches `Subnet.gateway_ip` and removes the sentinel. (`next_server` on line 55 has the same issue, though there legacy also stringifies.)
src/maasservicelayer/models/dhcp.py.61: `KeaHAConfig` needs the VLAN id (and IP version) it belongs to — see the comment on services/dhcp.py:273. As-is, `DHCPDataForAgent.ha_data` cannot be joined back to the subnets it configures.
src/maasservicelayer/models/dhcp.py.68: These dataclasses duplicate `DHCPDataForAgent`/`SubnetData`/`VlanData`/`InterfaceData`/`IPRangeData`/`HostReservationData` in `maastemporalworker/workflow/dhcp.py` with incompatible fields. Please link/track the cutover so the agent payload doesn't end up with two divergent definitions.

src/maasservicelayer/db/repositories/sta.106: This clause references `InterfaceTable` without declaring the join, unlike `with_interface_ids` just below it. It works only because `get_for_nodes` happens to join `maasserver_interface`; combined with plain `get_many` it silently emits a cross join. Add the `joins=[join(StaticIPAddressTable, InterfaceIPAddressTable, ...), join(InterfaceIPAddressTable, InterfaceTable, ...)]` chain so the clause is self-contained.

src/maasservicelayer/db/repositories/vla.50: Style: every other predicate in this factory uses the imported `eq(col, value)` helper. Use `or_(eq(VlanTable.c.primary_rack_id, rack_id), eq(VlanTable.c.secondary_rack_id, rack_id))` for consistency.

src/maasservicelayer/db/repositories/int.136: `_select_all_statement()` joins NodeConfig/Node/InterfaceIPAddress plus the IP subquery and aggregates `links` with a GROUP BY — all discarded here, since callers only need `name`/`mac_address`/`type`/`created`. `get_for_ip` (line 416) shows the cheaper pattern: `select(InterfaceTable)` joined to `InterfaceRelationshipTable` on `parent_id`, filtered by `child_id`, which also avoids the `IN (subquery)`.

src/maasservicelayer/services/interfaces.82: Every other method in this class goes through `self.interface_repository`; this one uses `self.repository`. They're the same object, but pick one — the inconsistency makes the class harder to read.
